title: Painting identity + info macros unported; paintings are purchasable and show raw %-macros
claim: DFU: DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:571 seeds message=Random.Range(0,65536) for Paintings; InitPaintingInfo (DaggerfallUnityItemMCP.cs:42-65) does DFRandom.srand(message), rand()%180 for file/record, GetPaintingRecordPart random_range_inclusive draws, and %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/%an each burn/draw rand() (all five registered in MacroHelper.cs). Port stocks paintings (shopStock.js:61 PawnShop pair 0x0D -> group 13 -> template 284, rarity 3, ~4%/shelf), routes Info to TEXT.RSC 250 (itemInfo.js:79), but expandItemInfo (itemInfo.js:191-204) handles no painting macro, paintings get no message seed, and grep for %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/InitPainting in src/ is empty.
consequence: Buy a painting at a pawn shop, click Info: the panel renders record 250 with unexpanded %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/%an (and likely all variant lines at once, where DFU picks one via DFRandom) instead of the classic generated painting description.

title: resetMagicRoundMarker never called: forward load fires up to 2880 spurious magic rounds
claim: DFU resets the broker's lastGameMinute on start AND load (InitMagicRoundTimer :817-823 'Called when game starts or loaded', plus LoadInProgress :206). The port's resetMagicRoundMarker (worldTick.js:608) has NO caller in src/. claimMagicRounds re-anchors only when the clock moved BACKWARDS (worldTick.js:119); its comment claims save.js re-anchors explicitly, but save.js:408 re-anchors only entity.lastGameMinutes, not the broker marker. worldQuickLoad (world.js:1654) sets the clock in-session with no marker reset, so a load to a LATER game time yields from = max(marker, to-2880) and a burst of up to 2880 rounds.
consequence: Loading a save ahead of the session clock instantly runs up to 2880 magic rounds: restored buffs expire on the spot, poisons burst, and a restored continuous-damage effect can kill on load.

verify.reason: EntityEffectBroker.cs:818-822 InitMagicRoundTimer resets lastGameMinute to the current clock on load, so DFU fires zero catch-up rounds on load. worldTick.js's resetMagicRoundMarker (:608) has no src/ caller (grep: test-only). claimMagicRounds (:110-123) only re-anchors on a BACKWARD jump (here < marker); worldQuickLoad (world.js:1654) advances the clock forward via setWorldMinutes without resetting the marker, and the next tick reads worldMinutes() (shared.js:735) into claimMagicRounds, yielding up to MAX_CATCHUP_ROUNDS=2880 (worldTick.js:586) spurious rounds on a forward load.

title: Region-condition store never minted at new game - PricesHigh/Low arms dead until first load
claim: createRegionConditions' only caller is restoreRegionConditions (regionConditions.js:188), reached only from save restore (save.js:395); no new-game path assigns entity.regionConditions (no other assignment exists in src/). worldTick passes `entity.regionConditions ?? null` (worldTick.js:253) and updateRegionalPrices skips the flag half on null (shopStock.js:309). DFU mints regionData at every new game (StartGameBehaviour.cs:433 -> InitializeRegionData, PlayerEntity.cs:2189-2211), so FormulaHelper.cs:2075-2087 writes PricesHigh/PricesLow from day one. save.js:392-394 even assumes a blank store 'is what InitializeRegionData mints at a new game anyway' - but nothing mints it.
consequence: In a session started fresh (no load), the shipped PricesHigh/PricesLow condition writes never execute and the first save records a blank condition store, diverging from DFU's save-relevant regionData flag state.

verify.reason: StartGameBehaviour.cs:433 calls InitializeRegionData() at new-game, minting regionData and writing PricesHigh/Low (PlayerEntity.cs:2189-2218). chargenSession.js never assigns entity.regionConditions; its only writer, restoreRegionConditions, runs solely from save.js:395 on load. worldTick.js:253 passes entity.regionConditions ?? null, and shopStock.js:309 `if (!conditions) continue;` skips the price-flag writes on null - verified directly. A fresh never-loaded character never gets the store or its flags.

title: Guild rank law reads live (enchant-modded) skill, DFU reads GetPermanentSkillValue
claim: Guild.CalculateNumHighLowSkills (Guild.cs:124) reads GetPermanentSkillValue, which excludes effect mods (DaggerfallSkills.cs:135-143 vs 176). The port's numHighLowSkills (guilds.js:202) calls skillValue (skills.js:60-71), which adds entity._enchantMods.skillMods[skillId] (skills.js:68) - the port's live mods channel, populated when the player equips an EnhancesSkill item (enchantments.js:655; DFU EnhancesSkill.cs:78 writes SetSkillMod, live-only). The file's own header (guilds.js:22-24) claims permanent reads. Feeds calculateNewRank, updateRank and isEligibleToJoin.
consequence: A player wearing an EnhancesSkill (+15) item on a guild skill can join or be promoted on skills their permanent values don't earn (and demoted on unequip); in DFU worn enchantments never move guild rank.

verify.reason: Guild.cs:124 reads GetPermanentSkillValue (DaggerfallSkills.cs:163-176, no mods), distinct from GetLiveSkillValue (:135-143, adds mods). Port's numHighLowSkills (guilds.js:199-207) calls skillValue (skills.js:60-71), which adds entity._enchantMods.skillMods[skillId] - populated by computeEnchantmentMods (enchantments.js:641-655) from worn EnhancesSkill items, DFU's live channel. guilds.js's own header (22-24) claims permanent reads, contradicting the code. No test pins _enchantMods against numHighLowSkills.

title: Training 'too skilled' gate compares live skill, DFU compares permanent
claim: TrainingSkill_OnItemPicked refuses training when GetPermanentSkillValue(skillToTrain) > GetTrainingMax (DaggerfallGuildServiceTraining.cs:101). The port's tooSkilledToTrain (guildServiceActions.js:108) uses skillValue(entity, skill), which folds entity._enchantMods.skillMods (skills.js:68), i.e. the live value including worn EnhancesSkill enchantments.
consequence: A player with permanent skill 40-50 wearing a +15 EnhancesSkill item is refused with 4022 ('too skilled') where DFU trains them; the 50-cap check moves with equipment.

verify.reason: DFU training (DaggerfallGuildServiceTraining.cs:101) gates on GetPermanentSkillValue, distinct from GetLiveSkillValue=permanent+mod (DaggerfallSkills.cs:135-138). Port's tooSkilledToTrain (guildServiceActions.js:104-108) calls skillValue() (skills.js:60-71) which always folds entity._enchantMods.skillMods -- the live value. Wired via ui/guildServiceWindows.js:216. No test covers the enchant-mod case.

title: Recipe picker part-fills the cauldron; DFU refuses on any missing ingredient and clears first
claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron builds a dict of required ingredients and, if ANY is unmatched, shows 'reqIngredients' and moves NOTHING (:298-300); only with all present does it ClearCauldron() (:304) then add the full set. The port's gatherRecipe comment claims DFU 'fills what it can... does not refuse the whole recipe for one missing herb', and the caller (ui/potionMakerWindow.js:184-194) adds the found subset on top of existing cauldron contents with no message and no clear. test/potions.test.js:179-188 pins the partial fill while citing the same C# lines — the pin restates the port, not the C#.
consequence: Picking a known recipe while missing one herb silently loads a partial cauldron; Mix then fails and consumes the herbs where DFU would have refused with a message and consumed nothing. Residual cauldron contents also pollute a fill instead of being cleared.

verify.reason: DaggerfallPotionMakerWindow.cs AddRecipeToCauldron:296-304: any unmatched ingredient shows 'reqIngredients' and moves nothing; full match only -> ClearCauldron() then add. Port gatherRecipe (potions.js:224-236) returns found/missing subsets and its comment misstates the C# behavior. Caller ui/potionMakerWindow.js _fillFrom:183-192 adds only `found` onto existing cauldron, no clear/no message. test/potions.test.js:178-188 pins this exact wrong behavior citing the true C# lines.

title: createArtifact never marks the artifact identified (DFU sets identifiedMask at mint)
claim: DFU SetArtifact writes `flags = artifactMask | identifiedMask` (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:617) so every artifact is born identified. The port's createArtifact (loot.js:280-295) sets artifact/magic/enchantments but never isIdentified, and no other producer does (only shopStock.js:484 and worldModes.js:774/782 write isIdentified). itemIsIdentified (tradeModes.js:130) requires isIdentified===true for any enchanted item, so every artifact reads UNIDENTIFIED.
consequence: expandItemInfo (itemInfo.js:186-189) drops an unidentified item's own name, so an artifact's info panel shows the base template name instead of the artifact name; the Identify service stages an artifact and charges (25*value)>>8 (tradeModes.js:244-251, 363) where DFU refuses (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:823-826).

verify.reason: DaggerfallUnityItem.cs SetArtifact:617 `flags = artifactMask | identifiedMask` - artifacts born identified; DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:823-826 Identify only transfers `if (!item.IsIdentified)`. Port's createArtifact (loot.js:266-296) never sets isIdentified; grep confirms only shopStock.js:484 and worldModes.js:774/782 do. tradeModes.js:130 itemIsIdentified requires isIdentified===true for enchanted items, so artifacts read unidentified; tradeModes.js:236-251/362-365 stage/charge them, itemInfo.js:186-189 drops their name.

title: Daedric quest offer crashes: _offerQuest dereferences this._guild which offerNamedQuest set to null
claim: offerNamedQuest (offerFlow.js:129-139) sets this._guild = null, then on a loaded quest calls _offerQuest(), which runs `if (this._guild.isMember())` (offerFlow.js:199) with no null guard - TypeError. In DFU the guild ExternalMCP assignment exists only in DaggerfallGuildServicePopupWindow.OfferQuest (:608) where guild is always non-null; the daedra path (DaggerfallQuestPopupWindow.cs:272-279) never touches a guild - DaggerfallDaedraSummonedWindow.cs:96-121 shows the offer. Live caller: worldModes.js:1675 -> offerDaedricQuest -> offerNamedQuest; daedra quest sources are vendored (vendor/dfu-quests/Quests/X0C00Y00.txt), so getQuest returns non-null and the crash line is reached.
consequence: First-time successful daedra summoning throws a TypeError instead of presenting the daedric quest offer; the quest can never be offered or accepted (gold already spent, Summoned flag already set).

verify.reason: offerFlow.js:132 offerNamedQuest sets this._guild=null, then on a real quest (vendor/dfu-quests/Quests/X0C00Y00.txt exists; questLists.js:111-112 returns it) calls _offerQuest() (line 139), which at line 199 does `if (this._guild.isMember())` with no null guard - TypeError. Live path: worldModes.js:1675 offerDaedricQuest, after gold deducted (:1660) and Summoned flag set (:1672), no surrounding try/catch. No test exercises the real-quest branch.
